text: ezGenomeTracks ggplot2-based R package genome browser-style track visualization. provides ez_*() wrappers (quick, high-level) geom_*() layers (full ggplot2 control).

title: ezGenomeTracks Helper
text: Every function needs region: "chr1:1000000-2000000". tracks figure must use region string x-axes align.

title: ezGenomeTracks Helper
text: ez_*() functions accept flexible input: - data frame genomic columns - file path (BED, bedGraph, bigWig, GTF, BEDPE …) - named list — creates multiple faceted sub-tracks

title: ezGenomeTracks Helper
text: Follow GRanges-style naming: | Column | Meaning | |—|—| | seqnames | chromosome, e.g. "chr1" | | start | start position (1-based) | | end | end position | | strand | "+", "-", "Unknown" — must factor levels c("minus","plus","Unknown") gene tracks | | score | numeric signal value (coverage, peak score, etc.) |

title: ezGenomeTracks Helper
text: ez_*() returns ggplot object — can add ggplot2 layers (+ theme(...), + labs(...)) top track.

title: ezGenomeTracks Helper
text: Plot signal intervals (bigWig, bedGraph, data frame seqnames/start/end/score). Key parameters: - type: "area" (default), "line", "heatmap" - colors: single color vector colors multiple tracks/groups - group_var: column name color within single data frame - y_axis_style: "none" (default) | "simple" | "minmax" | "full" - alpha: transparency (default 0.5) - average = TRUE: average multiple files one track - y_range: fix y-axis limits, e.g. c(0, 50)
code: library(ezGenomeTracks) region <- "chr1:100000-101000"  # From a data frame cov_df <- data.frame(   seqnames = "chr1",   start = seq(100000, 100990, by = 10),   end   = seq(100009, 100999, by = 10),   score = rnorm(100, 10, 2) ) track_cov <- ez_coverage(cov_df, region = region)  # From a file path track_cov <- ez_coverage("path/to/signal.bw", region = region)  # Multiple tracks via named list track_cov <- ez_coverage(   list(Sample1 = "s1.bw", Sample2 = "s2.bw"),   region = region,   colors = c("steelblue", "tomato") )

title: ezGenomeTracks Helper
text: Plot gene models GTF file, TxDb object, data frame. Key parameters: - label: column label genes (default "gene_name"); set label = NULL hide - label_style: "auto" | "repel" | "simple" | "none" - max_labels: limit number labels shown - exon_fill, exon_color, intron_color: explicit colors (bypasses strand-based coloring) - Default colors: plus strand = "green4", minus strand = "orange2" Strand factor levels pitfall: build data frame manually, use:
code: # From a data frame (must have seqnames, start, end, strand, type, gene_id, transcript_id) genes_df <- data.frame(   seqnames      = "chr1",   start         = c(100050, 100200),   end           = c(100150, 100350),   strand        = factor(c("+", "+"), levels = c("-", "+", "Unknown")),   type          = "exon",   gene_id       = "GENE1",   transcript_id = "TX1",   gene_name     = "GENE1" ) track_gene <- ez_gene(genes_df, region = region)  # From a GTF file (auto-imports with region filtering) track_gene <- ez_gene("genes.gtf", region = region)  # From a TxDb object library(TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38.knownGene) track_gene <- ez_gene(TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38.knownGene, region = region)  # Look up region by gene name instead of coordinates track_gene <- ez_gene(txdb, gene = "PTPRC", gene_db = txdb) strand = factor(strand_vec, levels = c("-", "+", "Unknown"))

title: ezGenomeTracks Helper
text: Plot genomic intervals rectangles (e.g. ChIP-seq peaks, regulatory elements). Key parameters: - fill: fill color (high end gradient use_score = TRUE) - color: border color (default "black") - alpha: transparency (default 0.7) - height: rectangle height 0–1 (default 0.8) - use_score: color-code score column (default FALSE)
code: features_df <- data.frame(   seqnames = "chr1",   start    = c(100120, 100300),   end      = c(100180, 100360),   score    = c(12, 8) ) track_feat <- ez_feature(features_df, region = region)  # Color by score (gradient) track_feat <- ez_feature(features_df, region = region,                          use_score = TRUE, fill = "darkred")  # From a BED file track_feat <- ez_feature("peaks.bed", region = region)

title: ezGenomeTracks Helper
text: Draw arcs pairs genomic intervals (enhancer–promoter contacts, etc.). Input data frame needs columns: chr1, start1, end1, chr2, start2, end2, optionally score. Key parameters: - direction: "" (default) | "" - curvature: arc curvature 0–1 (default 0.5) - size: line width (default 0.5) - use_score: color arcs score - colors: color vector colors
code: interactions_df <- data.frame(   chr1 = "chr1", start1 = 100120, end1 = 100160,   chr2 = "chr1", start2 = 100300, end2 = 100340,   score = 5 ) track_arc <- ez_link(interactions_df, region = region)  # Score-based coloring track_arc <- ez_link(interactions_df, region = region,                      use_score = TRUE, colors = "steelblue")

title: ezGenomeTracks Helper
text: Plot association statistics (e.g. GWAS -log10 p-values).
code: manhattan_df <- data.frame(   seqnames = rep("chr1", 50),   start    = seq(100000, 100000 + 49 * 200, by = 200),   end      = seq(100001, 100001 + 49 * 200, by = 200),   score    = rexp(50, rate = 0.3) ) track_manh <- ez_manhattan(manhattan_df, region = region)

title: ezGenomeTracks Helper
text: Plot binned pairwise contact frequencies triangular heatmap (default) square matrix. Input: sparse data frame seqnames, start1, start2, score; dense matrix; file path. Key parameters: - resolution: bin size bp (default 10000) - style: "triangle" (default) | "square" - palette: "cooler" (default) | "ylgnbu" | "viridis" | "bwr" - transform: "identity" | "log10" (default) | "log2" | "sqrt" - max_distance: trim triangle max interaction distance (bp)
code: hic_df <- tidyr::expand_grid(   bin1 = seq(100000, 100000 + 4 * 200, by = 200),   bin2 = seq(100000, 100000 + 4 * 200, by = 200) ) |>   dplyr::filter(bin2 >= bin1) |>   dplyr::mutate(score = runif(dplyr::n()), seqnames = "chr1") |>   dplyr::rename(start1 = bin1, start2 = bin2)  track_hic <- ez_hic(hic_df, region = region, resolution = 200)  # Square view track_hic <- ez_hic(hic_df, region = region, resolution = 200, style = "square")

title: ezGenomeTracks Helper
text: RNA-seq coverage + splice junction arcs one track. Key parameters: - junction_direction: "alternate" (default) | "" | "" - show_labels: show arc read-count labels (default TRUE) - score_transform: "identity" | "log10" | "sqrt" (scale arc thickness)
code: coverage <- data.frame(   seqnames = "chr1", start = 1:100, end = 2:101,   score = c(runif(30, 5, 10), rep(0, 20), runif(50, 5, 10)) ) junctions <- data.frame(   seqnames = "chr1", start = 30, end = 50, score = 15 ) track_sashimi <- ez_sashimi(coverage, junctions, "chr1:1-100")  # Multi-sample track_sashimi <- ez_sashimi(   coverage_data = list(S1 = cov1, S2 = cov2),   junction_data = list(S1 = junc1, S2 = junc2),   region = region,   colors = c("purple", "orange") )

title: Get started
text: several R/python packages plot genome browser tracks, require lot coding set . PygenomeTracks one favorite, requires writing .ini configuration files running command-line tools, can cumbersome R users, flexible generating large number plots exploratory data analysis. Using ggplot2, possible generate beautiful genome browser tracks, although typically requires lot custom code data wrangling. motivated create R package based ggplot2, providing simple high-level functions common track types. goal make easy create publication-quality genome browser plots minimal code users, still allowing advanced customization smaller number power users.

title: Get started
text: ezGenomeTracks designed around three core principles: modular ggplot2 geoms, simple high-level wrappers, consistent genomic scaling styling. package provides low-level building blocks advanced customization easy--use helpers quick plotting. Easy ez_* wrappers: common use-cases package provides ez_*() helper functions ez_coverage(), ez_gene(), ez_feature(). wrappers accept flexible input types (file paths, data.frame, GRanges, named lists) internally prepare data, select sensible defaults, return full ggplot2 layer complete track can stack vstack_plot(). imagine users primarily use high-level wrappers quick plotting. Custom Geoms: power users may want custom plots beyond ez_* wrappers can provide. case, package also exposes set geom_*() layers (e.g. geom_coverage(), geom_gene(), geom_feature(), geom_link(), geom_hic()). regular ggplot2 geoms can use directly ggplot() call. Genomic scales readable labels: Genomic coordinates can large hard read plotted directly. package provides scale_x_genome_region() related helpers transform coordinate labels human-friendly formats enforce consistent axis limits across stacked tracks. Key behaviors: Accepts region specification (string like “chr1:1000-2000” GRanges) sets x limits region stacked tracks share genomic window. Formats tick labels base pairs, kilobases (kb), megabases (Mb) appropriate axis labels compact readable. Optionally shows chromosome names relative offsets make cross-track alignment clear. Using scale_x_genome_region() keeps multi-track plots aligned makes numeric labels concise — e.g., 100,000 becomes 100 kb appropriate. Custom themes simple, pretty plots: package defines ez_theme() minimal base theme track-specific themes ez_coverage_theme() ez_gene_theme(). themes remove unnecessary gridlines, adjust margins, set clean defaults fonts, axis appearance, legend placement resulting tracks visually consistent publication-ready. Themes lightweight composable, can add override small pieces ggplot2 theme calls. Examples themes control: Background grid visibility Y-axis labeling tick formatting strand-aware tracks Default colors palettes Hi-C / interaction plots Spacing stacked tracks (via heights vstack_plot()) Example — applying themes tweaking appearance: Stacking tracks vertically vstack_plot(): Finally, vstack_plot() function takes list ggplot2 layers (ez_* wrappers custom geoms) stacks vertically single plot. handles aligning x-axes, applying themes, adjusting track heights cohesive multi-track visualization. believe powerful yet flexible way compose complex genome browser views allows user tinker individual tracks first combine seamlessly.
code: # one-line coverage track from a bigWig or data.frame cov <- ez_coverage(   "inst/extdata/example_signal.bedgraph",   region = "chr1:1009000-1092000",   colour = "steelblue" )  # one-line gene model track genes <- ez_gene(example_genes, region = "chr1:1009000-1092000")  # stack and display vstack_plot(list(cov, genes), region = "chr1:100000-101000") library(ggplot2) library(ezGenomeTracks)  # `signal_df` is a data frame with columns `seqnames`, `start`, `end`, `score` ggplot(signal_df) +   geom_coverage() +   scale_x_genome_region(region = "chr1:100000-101000") plot_list <- list(ez_coverage(example_signal), ez_gene(example_genes)) vstack_plot(plot_list, region = "chr2:50000-80000") +   scale_x_genome_region(region = "chr2:50000-80000") p <- ez_coverage(example_signal) + ez_coverage_theme() q <- ez_gene(example_genes) + ez_gene_theme()  vstack_plot(list(p, q), region = "chr1:100000-101000", heights = c(1, 0.8))

title: ezGenomeTracks
text: Region specification: always parse string like "chr1:100000-101000". Wrappers ez_*() accept data frames, file paths, lists apply proper geom + theme. tracks must share identical x-limits (region) composition. Standard columns follow GRanges style: seqnames, start, end, strand; plus type-specific columns (score, gene annotations, interaction endpoints).

title: ezGenomeTracks
text: numeric score intervals.
code: cov_df <- tibble::tibble(   seqnames = "chr1",   start = seq(100000, 100990, by = 10),   end = start + 9,   score = rnorm(length(start), 10, 2) ) track_cov <- ez_coverage(cov_df, region = region)

title: ezGenomeTracks

code: genes_df <- tibble::tibble(   seqnames = "chr1",   start = c(100050, 100200),   end   = c(100150, 100350),   strand = factor(c("plus", "plus"), levels = c("minus", "plus", "Unknown")),   type = "exon",   gene_id = "GENE1",   transcript_id = "TX1" ) track_gene <- ez_gene(genes_df, region = region)

title: ezGenomeTracks

code: features_df <- tibble::tibble(   seqnames = "chr1",   start = c(100120, 100300),   end   = c(100180, 100360),   score = c(12, 8) ) track_feat <- ez_feature(features_df, region = region)

title: ezGenomeTracks
text: Pairs genomic intervals (different chromosomes) drawn arcs.
code: interactions_df <- tibble::tibble(   chr1 = "chr1", start1 = 100120, end1 = 100160,   chr2 = "chr1", start2 = 100300, end2 = 100340,   score = 5 ) track_arc <- ez_arc(interactions_df, region = region)

title: ezGenomeTracks
text: Association results: point positions + score (e.g. -log10(p)).
code: manhattan_df <- tibble::tibble(   seqnames = rep("chr1", 50),   start = seq(100000, 100000 + 49*200, by = 200),   end = start + 1,   score = rexp(50, rate = 0.3) ) track_manh <- ez_manhattan(manhattan_df, region = region)

title: ezGenomeTracks
text: Binned pairwise contacts rendered triangular heatmap.
code: # Minimal synthetic example (x/y bins with a value) hic_df <- tidyr::expand_grid(   bin1 = seq(100000, 100000 + 4*200, by = 200),   bin2 = seq(100000, 100000 + 4*200, by = 200) ) |> dplyr::filter(bin2 >= bin1) |> dplyr::mutate(   score = runif(dplyr::n(), 0, 1),   seqnames = "chr1" ) |> dplyr::rename(start1 = bin1, start2 = bin2) track_hic <- ez_hic(hic_df, region = region)
